provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The output is built as a grid of blocks, one block per input cell, and each block is the size of the whole input. Block (i, j) gets a copy of the input when input cell (i, j) holds the marker colour. Every other block is filled with the background colour.

This rule behaves the same under every D4 transform. Rotating or reflecting the input turns the block layout and the copied tile by the same transform, so the program can work directly in visible coordinates with no direction-specific rewrite. Only the colour roles change. The marker becomes palette[5] and the fill becomes palette[0]. Both are baked in as constants.

The output canvas is (h*h) x (w*w). For the generator's square inputs this is exactly n^2 x n^2. It is also well-defined for rectangular grids.
draft_notes.limitations: The constructor only produces square inputs of size 3 to 5, so the rectangular handling is a natural extension that was never exercised. The empty-block colour is fixed to palette[0] rather than taken from the input's background. This matches pair 3, where the background is the marker but empty blocks are still 0. I found no fixture contradictions or constructor defects. The generator's symmetry latent ('angle') only shapes the input and is not needed by the rule.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Fractal self-tiling. For an n×n input, the output is n²×n². Block (i,j) is a copy of the whole input when input[i][j] equals the marker (5), and otherwise it is filled with 0. The emitted solver bakes in MARKER=palette[5] and FILL=palette[0]. It allocates np.full((h*h, w*w), FILL) and stamps g into out[i*h:(i+1)*h, j*w:(j+1)*w] wherever g[i,j]==MARKER, working directly on the visible grid.
evidence: Constructor output: common.grid(size*size, size*size) starts at 0. For each i with colors[i]==5 it writes output[row*size + j//size][col*size + j%size] = colors[j]. That is exactly block (row,col) = the full input. All other blocks stay 0. The factory solver computes the same thing, with h=w=size.

The four train fixtures and the test fixture are generated by the same constructor through explicit colors lists. Pair 3, whose background is 5, confirms that the fill is the constant 0 and not the input background. The factory's FILL=palette[0] matches this.

D4 equivariance holds. Take a symmetry T of the n×n input with induced index map (i,a) -> (i',a'). Applied to the n²×n² output, the global index i*n+a maps to i'*n+a'. For example, a vertical flip sends (n-1-i)*n + (n-1-a) to n²-1-(i*n+a). So the transformed output is the block layout under T with each block being T(input). This equals the solver applied to T(input). No untransform/native-solve/retransform wrapper is used.
There are no hidden-latent label dependencies. 'angle' and 'hues' only shape the input. The output depends only on the visible cell colours.

The fill colour is always visible in demonstration outputs. The generator's loop requires both hues to be present, so at least one cell is non-5 and at least one empty block exists. The marker is required to be present by the loop condition. Both roles are fixed constants shared across every pair, so no arbitrary per-episode lookup is involved.
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The constructor only emits square inputs of size 3–5. The solver's (h*h, w*w) handling of rectangular grids is unexercised.

The generator draws non-marker hues only from {1,2,3} plus 0. Under palette permutation, other colours are never present as non-marker content. The solver treats every non-marker colour uniformly, so this does not affect correctness.

The fill is fixed to palette[0] rather than inferred. This is justified by pair 3, where the background is the marker yet empty blocks are 0. It is consistent with every fixture and with the constructor.
The symmetric-placement loop can overwrite cells, so inputs vary in how much symmetry they keep. The rule is unaffected because the output depends only on the final visible colours.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the palette augmentation is a bijection, so that no non-marker colour can map onto palette[5]. A non-bijective map would make marker identification ambiguous.
No colour-association evidence check applies: ad7e01d0 is not in the require_colour_evidence task list, and the marker and fill roles are fixed constants that are visible in every demonstration.

draft_notes.host_review: Reviewed rule and domain limitations. Host augmentation maps completed grids with one bijective palette, horizontal reflection then clockwise quarter turns; odd indices swap axes. Fresh audit iterates all eight variants, supplied fixture checks include query answers, and export requires every pair exact. Sampler exceptions are recorded rejections, not admitted examples. Spatial connectivity follows the stated constructor/archived mechanism; optional out-of-domain modes are not certified.
